derivation_provenance.method: every value below was produced by decimal arithmetic on the constants in parameters/ and on the declared composition and activity data in model/graph.json, before any builder or solver ran; the independent re-derivation lives in tmp/segment9h_30_steel_recipe.py and its literal dump in tmp/segment9h_31_steel_numbers.json
derivation_provenance.independence: no value in this file was copied from a bundle, a builder print or an engine result; the comparison direction is always result-to-here

tolerance_default.reason: authored amounts carry six decimal places

derivation_provenance.arithmetic_environment: Python decimal module, precision 25 significant digits, no floating point
derivation_provenance.published_ratios: carbon to CO2 is the published f = 3,664 t CO2/t C of Annex II's mass balance method (parameters/carbon-content.json#published_constants/f_CO2_over_C, @105374), so a carbon mass is multiplied by that literal rather than by the atomic ratio 44.009/12.011 = 3.664057946882024810590292. Carbonate decomposition uses the published 0,440 t CO2/t CaCO3 of Annex II point G Table 3 rather than the atomic 0.4397118478108826409288012. Both slacks are named as MFA residual terms rather than absorbed

functional_unit_result.name: specific_embedded_emissions
functional_unit_result.two_readings_rule: expected is the sum of the derived component values while authored_sum is the sum of the six decimal amounts the model stores. They differ by 3.43950632674687e-10, which is the rounding of the two blast furnace terms alone, so an engine result must sit within the stated tolerance of expected and must equal authored_sum exactly when the stored amounts are added as stored.
functional_unit_result.value_equality_note: kg CO2 per kg crude steel and t CO2 per t crude steel are the same number, so the kg to tonne conversion of ST-01 must not scale this result; it divides the numerator and the denominator by the same 1000

numerator_at_declared_activity_level.derivation: the six authored component amounts added as stored: 193.4592 + 74.448 + 524.748873 + 976.902701 + 152.56896 + 18.612, which is the numerator the model carries before the per-tonne reading divides it by the 1000 kg slab of ST-16
numerator_at_declared_activity_level.reading: the method package cross-checks the solved numerator in kg against this field, not against the per-tonne value, because the solver returns the exchanges of a 1000 kg activity in kg

activity_level.rule: the denominator is the cast slab that leaves the production process, not the sum of the five process outputs; the 20 kg casting crop is excluded from it by ST-16 and appears in the mass account only

terms.derivation: carbon of 60 kg coke breeze at 88 % C = 52.800 kg C, times the published 3,664 t CO2/t C, over 1000 kg of slab
169.200 kg CaCO3 in 180 kg of sinter lime at 94 %, times the published 0,440 t CO2/t CaCO3

carbon that carries the ore lattice oxygen out as CO2: the sinter lattice oxygen of 386.760677 kg minus the 5.229291 kg that bonds the iron oxidised into the furnace slag = 381.531386 kg O, divided by (f - 1) = 2.664 and times f, giving 143.217487 kg C and 524.748873 kg CO2

the rest of the furnace carbon budget: coke 344.000 kg C + PCI 101.400 kg C + methane 5.989403 kg C - the 41.550 kg C that stays in the hot metal = 409.839403 kg C in the top-gas carbon, minus the 143.217487 kg C of the reduction term above, giving 266.621916 kg C times f
carbon burnt by the lance: hot metal 41.550 kg C + scrap 0.600 kg C - the 0.510 kg C that stays in the treated steel of ST-16 = 41.640 kg C, times the published 3,664 t CO2/t C
42.300 kg CaCO3 in 45 kg of converter flux at 94 %, times the published 0,440 t CO2/t CaCO3

carbon_budget.note: the injected gas carbon is the methane carbon of 8 kg of CH4 on the 12.011/16.043 basis, and the treated steel keeps both the slab carbon and the cutting-loss carbon because ST-16 takes the crop out of the activity level but not out of the converter bath

absent_components.reason: none of the eight boundary-crossing material and energy inputs of this model is a good on the Annex I list once the 7204 scrap exception and the in-house sinter and hot metal of ST-15 are read, so the precursor bucket is empty and the good is simple; an empty bucket must not appear as a zero-weight component row

Annex II makes electricity indirect emissions non-attributable for this aggregated goods category, so a component row here would restate a term the law excludes; the 600 MJ and 25 MJ of grid electricity stay visible as activity data and as excluded candidates in boundaries/cbam.json

role_attribution.rule: the CBAM result must remain decomposable per production process, because a total that is right for the wrong reason cannot be audited

expected_per_process.note: this process carries no emission port of its own in the first version, which is modeling gap MG-S09 rather than a claim that it emits nothing
same reading as secondary metallurgy: its 25 MJ of electricity is excluded by ST-12, so its direct term is empty by clause

role_attribution.sum_check: 267.9072 + 1501.651574 + 171.18096 = 1940.739734 kg CO2, which is the numerator of the functional unit result

coverage_detector.purpose: prove that the three strands of the route can no longer be dropped silently, which is the failure mode of the pre-repair steel snapshots
coverage_detector.expected_if_sintering_strand_missing: 1.672832534 t CO2/t, i.e. the total minus 0.2679072
coverage_detector.expected_if_converter_flux_missing: 1.922127734 t CO2/t, i.e. the total minus 0.018612
coverage_detector.rule: a result equal to either figure must fail acceptance with the missing process or exchange named, and a coverage report that omits a counted exchange without a clause reference must fail before calculation
coverage_detector.historical_comparison: no regenerated result from cases/petrochemical-refinery-reference may present the blast furnace strand alone as complete coverage of CN 7207

foreground_boundary_co2.derivation: sum of the same six characterised exchanges over the same 1000 kg activity level
foreground_boundary_co2.coverage: partial by clause, not partial by omission: boundaries/pcf.json states which background strands are absent (upstream ore, coke and scrap production, the grid emission factor of the 625 MJ, and the unported air and lance oxygen of MG-S09), so a figure from this seed is a foreground-boundary value and is reported as such
foreground_boundary_co2.relation_to_cbam: the foreground boundary term is the same number as the CBAM direct component, and the build gate proves it rather than describing it, because it compares pcf.foreground_boundary_co2 with the direct term of the ledger

residual_explanation.reading: the model takes in less mass than it appears to output because the blast air, the lance oxygen and the ore lattice oxygen it consumes are not authored as input ports, and because the published carbonate factor is slightly larger than the atomic residue that stays in the slag. Each of those is a named term with a gap reference; none of them is a balancing plug, and a residual that vanishes without these terms is a wrong result rather than an improved balance.

energy_is_never_mass.rule: an MJ amount must not appear inside either kg sum, and must not be reported as a mass residual

elementary_flow_count.rule: six fossil CO2 exchanges, two per emission-bearing process; a seventh whose carbon origin is coke, breeze, PCI coal, injected gas or flux already counted must be rejected as a double count

mass_and_atom_checks.name: sinter_is_hematite_plus_gangue_plus_additions
mass_and_atom_checks.expected: 1490 kg ore = 900 kg Fe + 386.760677 kg lattice oxygen (3 x 15.999 / 2 / 55.845 per kg Fe) + 203.239323 kg gangue; the sinter retains the lattice oxygen it keeps and loses only the CO2 of its breeze and carbonate

mass_and_atom_checks.name: furnace_iron_splits
mass_and_atom_checks.expected: 900 kg Fe of the sinter = 881.747 kg Fe in hot metal + 18.253 kg Fe oxidised into the furnace slag

mass_and_atom_checks.name: furnace_carbon_budget
mass_and_atom_checks.expected: the furnace carbon in (coke + PCI + methane) minus the carbon of the hot metal splits exactly between the reduction term and the raceway term

mass_and_atom_checks.name: converter_iron_and_carbon_closure
mass_and_atom_checks.expected: hot metal iron + scrap iron = liquid steel iron + iron oxidised into converter slag, and hot metal carbon + scrap carbon = liquid steel carbon + burnt carbon

mass_and_atom_checks.name: casting_treatment_mass
mass_and_atom_checks.expected: 1020 kg treated steel = 1000 kg slab + 20 kg cutting crop, and secondary metallurgy and casting each close at 1020 kg in and 1020 kg out

mass_and_atom_checks.name: no_route_mixing
mass_and_atom_checks.expected: no node of this graph is an electric arc furnace and no port carries electrode or DRI mass, because ST-06 separates the two routes and section 3 of this seed ships the blast furnace branch only
mass_and_atom_checks.forbidden: a scrap input larger than the converter's cooling allowance, or an electricity demand that could belong to an EAF

explicit_non_assertions: these values are not an installation measurement and not a filing value; they are a self-consistent BF-BOF recipe at a declared composition, authored to exercise the boundary
a match between an engine result and this file proves the arithmetic and the boundary wiring, not regulatory compliance
the default-value route of ST-15 is not exercised here because its numbers were never retrieved, which is gap GS-01 and modeling gap MG-S05
exported blast furnace, coke oven and converter gas are not modelled, so the numerator must be read as a conservative upper bound for a plant that sells gas out, which is modeling gap MG-S11
no acceptance criterion here depends on resolving modeling gaps MG-S01 to MG-S11; they are reported alongside the result
